location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| Aspect | What Turbonomic Provides | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|--------|--------------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Visibility** | A single pane of glass that aggregates metrics, logs, and performance data across all clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP) and on‑prem environments. | Unilever can see real‑time resource utilization, application health, and cost signals without switching dashboards or pulling data manually. |
| **Predictive Analytics & AI Recommendations** | Uses machine learning models to predict future capacity needs, detect anomalies, and recommend actions (scale up/down, move workloads, right‑size instances). | Enables proactive optimization—Unilever can avoid over‑provisioning, reduce waste, and ensure SLA compliance before problems occur. |
| **Automated Remediation** | Executes recommended actions automatically or via APIs/automation workflows (Terraform, Ansible, etc.). | Frees operations teams from manual tuning; Unilever can focus on higher‑value tasks while maintaining optimal performance and cost. |
| **Cost Management & Chargeback** | Tracks spend per business unit, project, or team, and provides chargeback/showback reports. | Gives Unilever clear insight into where money is being spent and allows finance to allocate budgets accurately. |
| **Policy‑Based Governance** | Lets you define policies (performance thresholds, budget limits, compliance rules) that are enforced automatically. | Ensures Unilever’s IT governance and regulatory requirements are met consistently across all clouds. |
| **Integration Ecosystem** | Connects to Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring tools (Prometheus, Datadog), and ticketing systems (Jira, ServiceNow). | Seamlessly fits into Unilever’s existing DevOps workflow, enabling continuous optimization. |

---

### Key Differences Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Provider Tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | Native Cloud Tool (GCP, AWS, Azure) |
|---------|------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + hybrid (on‑prem, edge) | Limited to its own ecosystem |
| **Data Aggregation** | Pulls telemetry from multiple sources (VMs, containers, databases, network devices) | Primarily collects data from within its own services |
| **Analytics Engine** | Proprietary ML models that learn workload behavior over time | Basic dashboards, alerts, and limited predictive capabilities |
| **Automation** | Executes recommendations via APIs, Terraform, Ansible, or custom scripts | Automation is usually provider‑specific (e.g., AWS Lambda, Azure Logic Apps) |
| **Governance** | Policy engine that spans all resources regardless of provider | Policies are confined to each provider’s native IAM/management console |
| **Chargeback/Showback** | Built‑in cost allocation and reporting across all clouds | Cost allocation requires separate tools or manual tagging |
| **Vendor Lock‑In Risk** | Vendor‑agnostic platform – no lock‑in to a single cloud | Using only native tools ties you to that vendor’s ecosystem |
| **Learning Curve** | Requires training but offers unified UI and API | Each provider has its own UI, CLI, and terminology |

---

#### Bottom Line for Unilever

*Turbonomic acts as a **single control plane** that brings together disparate data streams, applies AI to uncover hidden inefficiencies, and enforces policies automatically. While native cloud tools excel at deep integration within their own ecosystems, they lack the cross‑cloud perspective and unified automation that Turbonomic delivers.*
